<ns0:div xmlns:ns0="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29" type="chapter">
                  <ns0:head>CHAP. XXIX.</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p n="1">1 FUrthermore, David the king said unto all the congregation, Solomon my son, whom a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lone God hath chosen, <ns0:hi>is yet</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ch. 22. 5.</ns0:note> young and tender <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Comparatively: for he was now married, as appears by com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />paring 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 9. 30. and 12. 13.</ns0:note>, and the work <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> great: for the palace <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> not for man, but for the LORD.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:342" />2 Now I have prepared with all my might for the house of my God, the gold for <ns0:hi>things to be made</ns0:hi> of gold, and the silver for <ns0:hi>things</ns0:hi> of silver, and the brass for <ns0:hi>things</ns0:hi> of brass, the iron for <ns0:hi>things</ns0:hi> of iron, and wood for things of wood; onyx-stones, and <ns0:hi>stones</ns0:hi> to be set <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Diamonds, or Emeraulds, or Rubies, or any of those pretious Stones which are usually set in Rings or such things.</ns0:note>, glistering stones, and of divers colours, and all manner of precious stones, and marble-stones in abundance.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3 Moreover, because I have set my affection to the house of my God, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> there is to me a pecu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />liar treasure.</ns0:note> I have of mine own pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />per good <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Of that which I had reserved as a peculiar Treasure to my own Use, after I had separated those things which I had devoted to God.</ns0:note>, of gold and silver, <ns0:hi>which</ns0:hi> I have given to the house of my God, over and above all that I have prepared for the holy house,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4 <ns0:hi>Even</ns0:hi> three thousand talents of gold, of the gold of <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Kin. 9. 28.</ns0:note> Ophir <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Which was accounted the best and purest Gold: of which see <ns0:hi>Iob.</ns0:hi> 22. 24. & 28. 16. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 13. 12. By which it appears that those 100000 Talents mentioned before, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 22. 14. were a courser and impurer sort of Gold.</ns0:note>, and seven thousand talents of refined silver, to overlay the walls of the houses <ns0:hi>withal</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The Walls of the Temple with Gold, and of the Rooms adjoyning to it with Silver beaten out into Plates and put upon the other Materials here and there as it was thought fit.</ns0:note>:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 The gold for <ns0:hi>things</ns0:hi> of gold, and the silver for <ns0:hi>things</ns0:hi> of silver, and for all manner of work <ns0:hi>to be made</ns0:hi> by the hands of artificers. And who <ns0:hi>then</ns0:hi> is willing, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">

                  <ns0:p n="6">6 Then the chief of the <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>families. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">

                           </ns0:gap>
                        </ns0:hi> Gr.</ns0:note> fathers and princes of the tribes of Israel, and the captains of thousands and of hundreds, with the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ch. 27. 25.</ns0:note> rulers over the kings <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> substance.</ns0:note> work, offered willingly,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 And gave for the service of the house of God, of gold five thousand talents, and ten thousand drams, and of silver ten thousand talents; and of brass, eighteen thousand talents, and one hundred thousand talents of iron.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 And they with whom <ns0:hi>precious</ns0:hi> stones were found, gave <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> to the treasure of the house of the LORD, by the hand of <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ch. 26. 21.</ns0:note> Jehiel the Gershonite.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 Then the people rejoyced <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Because this was both an Effect of Gods Grace in them, and an Eminent Token of Gods Favour and Goodness to be continued to them, and a good Pledge that this great and long-desired Work of the building of the Temple would receive a certain and a speedy Accomplishment.</ns0:note>, for that they offered willingly because with perfect heart they offered willingly to the LORD: and David the king also rejoyced with great joy.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 Wherefore David blessed the LORD before all the congregation; and David said, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Gr.</ns0:hi> thou art to be blessed.</ns0:note> Blessed <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> thou, LORD God of Israel our father, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">

                  <ns0:p n="11">11 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 6. 13. 1 Tim. 1. 17. Rev. 5. 13.</ns0:note> Thine, O LORD <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the greatness, and the power <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Thou art Great, and Powerful, &c.</ns0:note>, and the glory, and the victory, and the majesty: for all <ns0:hi>that is</ns0:hi> in the heaven, and in the earth, <ns0:hi>is thine;</ns0:hi> thine <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the kingdom, O LORD, and thou art exalted as head above all <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">As the Soveraign Lord and Owner of all Persons and Things.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12 Both riches and honour <ns0:hi>come</ns0:hi> of thee, and thou reignest over all <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">

                  <ns0:p n="13">13 Now therefore, our God, we thank thee, and praise thy glorious name.</ns0:p>

For the Land which we possess is thine, not ours, we are not the Proprietors or perpetual Possessors of it, but onely thy Tenants: and as our Fathers once were meer <ns0:hi>strangers</ns0:hi> in it, even with or be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore men, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 105. 12. so we at this day are no better with or be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore thee, having no absolute Right and Title in it, but onely to travel through it, and sojourn in it for that short time <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">

                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:note> abiding <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">We onely give to thee what we must shortly leave, and what we cannot keep to our selves: and there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore it is a great Favour that <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> wilst accept such Offerings; or, and therefore we are not perpetual Possessors of this Land and the Fruits of it, but onely Pilgrims and Passengers thorough it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 O LORD our God, all this store that we have prepared to build thee an house for thine holy name, <ns0:hi>cometh</ns0:hi> of thine hand, and <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> all thine own.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">17 I know also, my God, that thou <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">

                        </ns0:gap> 
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">

                        </ns0:gap>

                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:note> triest the heart, and hast pleasure in uprightness. As for me, in the uprightness of mine heart I have willingly offered all these things: and now have I seen with joy thy people which are <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>

                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:note> present here, to offer willingly unto thee <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">By the largeness of their Offering I dis<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ern the Sincerity, Wil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lingness and Generosity of their Hearts towards thee: for David judged, as in reason and charity he ought, of the Tree by its Fruit, and of their Hearts by their Actions.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="18">18 O LORD God of Abraham, Isaac, and of Israel our father, keep this for ever in the imagina<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of the thoughts of the heart of thy people <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Since it is from thy Grace that thy People have such willing Minds to thy Service, as was before acknowledged, I beg the con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tinuance of that Grac<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">

                        </ns0:gap> to them, that they may persist in the s<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">

                  <ns0:p n="19">19 And give unto Solomon my son a perfect heart to keep thy commandments, thy testimonies and thy statutes, and to do all <ns0:hi>these things,</ns0:hi> and to build the palace <ns0:hi>for</ns0:hi> the which I have made provision <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">By purchasing the Place, 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 21. and providing for the Expences of the Work.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="20">20 And David said to all the congregation, Now bless the LORD your God. And all the congregati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on blessed the LORD God of their fathers, and bowed down their heads, and worshipped the LORD and the king <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">The Lord with Religious, and the King with Civil, Worship, as it is evident.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="21">21 And they sacrificed sacrifices unto the LORD <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Before the Ark, which was there.</ns0:note>, and offered burnt-offerings unto the LORD, on the morrow after that day, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> a thou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sand bullocks, a thousand rams, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> a thousand lambs, with their drink-offerings, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Either 1. on the behalf of all Israel, to praise God in their Names, to procure Gods Pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sence and Blessing for them all. Or 2. so many, that the Feasts which, after the manner, were made of the remainders of the Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crifices, were abundantly sufficient for all the Israelites which were then present and desired to partake of them; or for all the Gover<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nours of Israel there assembled, who may well pas<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">

                  <ns0:p n="22">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:342" />22 And did eat and drink before the LORD <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Before the Ark, in Courts or Places as near to it as they conveniently could. Or, as in Gods Presence, in a Solemn and Religious manner, praising God for this great Mercy, and begging his Blessing upon this great Affair.</ns0:note> on that day with great gladness, and they made So<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lomon the son of David king the second time <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">This is called the <ns0:hi>second time</ns0:hi> in reference to the first time, which was either 1. when he was made King during <ns0:hi>Adonijahs</ns0:hi> Conspiracy, of which see 1 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 1. 34, &c. And so this was done after <ns0:hi>Davids</ns0:hi> death, and not up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on <ns0:hi>that day,</ns0:hi> when this Feasting and Solemnity lasted, as the words at first view seem to insinuate, this being related in the same verse, and immediately after the Relation of the Feast. But there are Examples of things done at distant times put together in one verse, as <ns0:hi>Act</ns0:hi> 7. 15. <ns0:hi>So Iacob went down into Egypt, and died, he and our Fathers, i. e</ns0:hi> first <ns0:hi>he, and</ns0:hi> afterward <ns0:hi>our Fathers.</ns0:hi> So here, <ns0:hi>They did eat——on that day with great gladness, and</ns0:hi> afterward <ns0:hi>they made Solomon—king the second time.</ns0:hi> And this Opinion seems to be confirmed by the following Passages, in which it is re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lated that at this same time <ns0:hi>they anointed Zadok to be Priest,</ns0:hi> and that Solomon was <ns0:hi>King instead of David,</ns0:hi> and that <ns0:hi>all Israel,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>all Davids sons submitted to him:</ns0:hi> All which was not done till after Davids death, as may be gathered by comparing this with 1 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 1. & 2. <ns0:hi>or</ns0:hi> 2. in 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 23. 1. where it is said that <ns0:hi>David—made Solomon his Son King over Israel; i. e.</ns0:hi> he declared him his Successor. And so this <ns0:hi>second time</ns0:hi> was during Davids Life. And what David had more privately declared, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 23. he now more so<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lemnly owns in this great and general Assembly, in which by Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vids Order and the Consent of all that Assembly Solomon was a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nointed King, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> to be King after his Fathers death. And this Opinion the Text seems most to favour. For it is said, <ns0:hi>And they made Solomon King,</ns0:hi> &c. <ns0:hi>they,</ns0:hi> who? That must be fetched out of the foregoing Words and Verses, <ns0:hi>they</ns0:hi> who <ns0:hi>did eat and drink before the Lord on that day with great gladness,</ns0:hi> as it is here said, and then immediately it follows, and that with a copulative conjunction, <ns0:hi>and they made Solomon King,</ns0:hi> &c. which without violence cannot be pulled away from the foregoing Words.
